objects.description: No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only declares functions operating on C strings. Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.

functions.name: fsearch_string_is_empty
functions.description: Returns whether the given C string is empty. Intended to be used to quickly check if a string has no characters. Exact handling of NULL is not documented; assume it expects a valid, null-terminated string.
requirements: str must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Behavior for str == NULL is unknown and not documented.

functions.name: fsearch_string_has_upper
functions.description: Returns true if the given C string contains at least one uppercase character. Expected for ASCII/locale-agnostic checks; exact character class and locale handling are not documented.
requirements: str must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Character set and locale handling are unknown; do not assume Unicode-aware semantics.

functions.name: fsearch_string_get_extension
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the file-extension portion of the given path or filename string (e.g., substring after the last dot). Specifics such as whether the dot is included, how paths like ".bashrc" or names with multiple dots are handled, and whether the returned pointer refers to the input buffer or a separate allocation are not documented.
requirements: str must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Returned pointer ownership and lifetime are unknown; treat it as referencing within str unless documented otherwise.
Behavior for inputs without a dot, leading dots, or trailing dots is unspecified.

functions.name: fsearch_string_utf8_has_upper
functions.description: Returns true if the UTF-8 encoded string contains at least one uppercase character. Intended for Unicode-aware uppercase detection. Exact Unicode version, normalization, and locale handling are not documented.
requirements: str must be a valid, null-terminated UTF-8 string.
Behavior for invalid UTF-8 sequences is unspecified.
Exact definition of “uppercase” is unspecified (Unicode properties and normalization are not documented).

functions.name: fsearch_string_is_ascii_icase
functions.description: Detects if str is composed purely of ASCII characters in both its lower and upper case form (per the header comment). Useful to determine if case-folding can be safely done using ASCII rules. Exact interpretation beyond the comment is not documented.
requirements: str must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Only ASCII content is considered; behavior with non-ASCII bytes is unspecified.

functions.name: fsearch_string_has_wildcards
functions.description: Returns true if the string contains wildcard characters. Based on adjacent documentation for wildcard-to-regex conversion, this likely refers to '*' and '?' but exact set is not documented.
requirements: str must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Exact set of characters considered “wildcards” is not explicitly documented.

functions.name: fsearch_string_convert_wildcard_to_regex_expression
functions.description: Converts a wildcard expression to a regular expression: '*' becomes '.*', '?' becomes '.', and other regex metacharacters are properly escaped. Intended for preparing a regex pattern from a shell-style wildcard input. Memory ownership of the returned string is not documented.
requirements: str must be a valid, null-terminated C string containing the wildcard expression.
Only the '*' and '?' wildcard semantics are documented; other wildcard conventions are not specified.
The function returns a char* to the resulting regex; allocation/ownership and required deallocation (e.g., via free) are not documented and therefore unknown.

functions.name: fsearch_string_starts_with_interval
functions.description: Detects if str starts with an interval identifier (i.e., ".." or "-"). On success, sets *end_ptr to the first character after the interval; otherwise sets *end_ptr to str. Useful for parsing range or interval prefixes.
requirements: str must be a valid, mutable, null-terminated C string.
end_ptr must be a non-NULL pointer to a char* variable that the function can set.
On return, *end_ptr points into the passed str buffer (either after the interval or to str itself).
Exact set of supported interval syntaxes is limited to those documented (".." and "-"). Behavior with other prefixes is unspecified.

data_types.description: A C-style byte string ending with a single NUL (\0) terminator. May contain arbitrary bytes except interior NULs. Used wherever the API expects const char* or char* C strings.

A C-style string representing a filename or filesystem path, potentially including directories, dots, and separators. It is not required to be a valid existing path; it is used for parsing components like extensions.
A valid, null-terminated UTF-8 encoded text string. Should contain well-formed UTF-8 byte sequences. May include ASCII as a subset.
A null-terminated string consisting solely of 7-bit ASCII characters (bytes 0x01–0x7F), with no interior NULs.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator creates valid null-terminated C strings representing filenames/paths
# to exercise fsearch_string_get_extension. We aim to cover many edge cases: no dot,
# single/multiple dots, leading dots (.bashrc), trailing dots (file.), hidden dirs,
# Windows and POSIX separators, mixed Unicode in UTF-8, long names, spaces, and
# special characters commonly seen in filenames.

ASCII_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_@# $"
WIN_SEP = "\\"
POSIX_SEP = "/"

# Some hand-crafted interesting samples
TEMPLATES: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty string
    ".",  # single dot (current dir)
    "..",  # parent dir
    ".bashrc",  # leading dot no extension?
    "file",  # no dot
    "file.txt",  # simple extension
    "archive.tar.gz",  # multiple dots
    "file.",  # trailing dot
    ".hidden.",  # leading + trailing dots
    "C:" + WIN_SEP + "path" + WIN_SEP + "file.ext",  # Windows drive path
    POSIX_SEP + "usr" + POSIX_SEP + "bin" + POSIX_SEP + "script.sh",  # POSIX path
    POSIX_SEP + "home" + POSIX_SEP + ".config" + POSIX_SEP + "app",  # hidden dir, no ext
    POSIX_SEP + "home" + POSIX_SEP + ".config" + POSIX_SEP + "app.conf",  # hidden dir + ext
    "file.name.with.many.dots.ext",  # many dots
    "noext" + POSIX_SEP + "folder",  # path ending in folder (no dot)
    "traildot" + POSIX_SEP + "dir." + POSIX_SEP + "file",  # dot in dir
    "mix.seps" + POSIX_SEP + "sub" + WIN_SEP + "file.txt",  # mixed seps
    "emoji_📄.txt",  # UTF-8 in base name
    "résumé.pdf",  # UTF-8 accents
    "空间/文件.扩展",  # CJK path and extension
    "a.b",  # minimal ext
    ".a.b",  # leading dot then dot
    "...",  # only dots
    "name..ext",  # double dot before ext
    "file.tar.gz.sig",  # deep extension
    "tricky..",  # ends with double dot
]

UNICODE_PARTS = [
    "📁", "📄", "🧪", "Δ", "λ", "ß", "ñ", "ø", "ç", "Ž", "漢字", "テスト", "список",
]

EXTENSIONS_COMMON = [
    "txt", "c", "h", "cpp", "hpp", "py", "json", "xml", "html", "gz", "tar", "zip", "7z",
    "mp3", "jpg", "png", "pdf", "conf", "ini", "log", "so", "dll", "exe", "sh",
]

DIR_NAMES = [
    "src", "bin", "lib", "include", ".git", ".config", "build", "temp", "var", "etc", "home",
]

def rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(n))

def rand_unicode(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    parts = []
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    for _ in range(n):
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(r.choice(UNICODE_PARTS))
        else:
            parts.append(r.choice(ASCII_SAFE))
    return "".join(parts)

def build_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Randomly construct Windows or POSIX style path
    use_windows = r.random() < 0.3
    sep = WIN_SEP if use_windows else POSIX_SEP

    parts: List[str] = []

    # Optional drive on Windows
    if use_windows and r.random() < 0.5:
        drive = chr(ord('A') + r.randint(0, 25)) + ":" + sep
        parts.append(drive)

    # Optional leading separator for absolute POSIX
    if not use_windows and r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(sep)

    # Build some directories
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)):
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append(r.choice(DIR_NAMES))
        elif r.random() < 0.5:
            # hidden dir
            parts.append("." + rand_ascii(r, 1, 6))
        else:
            parts.append(rand_unicode(r, 1, 8))
        parts.append(sep)

    # Filename/base
    base_choice = r.random()
    if base_choice < 0.15:
        base = ""  # allow empty last component (path ending with sep handled by caller)
    elif base_choice < 0.3:
        base = "." * r.randint(1, 3)  # dots only
    else:
        # Hidden file or normal
        prefix = "." if r.random() < 0.2 else ""
        core = rand_unicode(r, 1, 12)
        base = prefix + core

    # Extension patterns
    ext_mode = r.random()
    if ext_mode < 0.25:
        # no extension
        pass
    elif ext_mode < 0.5:
        base += "."
    elif ext_mode < 0.8:
        base += "." + r.choice(EXTENSIONS_COMMON)
    else:
        # multiple chained extensions
        for _ in range(r.randint(2, 4)):
            if r.random() < 0.2:
                # empty segment to create sequences like name..ext
                base += "."
            base += "." + r.choice(EXTENSIONS_COMMON)

    parts.append(base)

    # Optionally add trailing separator or trailing dots
    tail = r.random()
    if tail < 0.1:
        parts.append(sep)
    elif tail < 0.2:
        parts.append(".")

    # Join carefully: parts list may contain separators as standalone items or inside components
    # We join by empty string since we explicitly place seps as separate entries
    path = "".join(parts)
    return path

def choose_sample(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose between handcrafted templates and randomly composed paths
    if r.random() < 0.45:
        return r.choice(TEMPLATES)
    else:
        return build_path(r)


def clamp_size(b: bytes, limit: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    if len(b) <= limit:
        return b
    # Ensure we cut at a code point boundary for UTF-8 where possible:
    # Trim and then backtrack until valid utf-8 or minimal size
    data = bytearray(b[:limit])
    # Try to decode; if fails, back off a few bytes (C side only needs NUL terminated, so it's fine)
    for back in range(0, 4):
        try:
            _ = data[: limit - back].decode('utf-8')
            return bytes(data[: limit - back])
        except Exception:
            continue
    return bytes(data)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    s = choose_sample(r)
    # Ensure null-terminated C string contract by appending a single NUL when fuzzing harness copies
    # The fuzzer stub adds its own NUL, but our buffer should not contain embedded NULs unless intended.
    # We avoid internal NULs; all characters chosen are non-NUL.
    data = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    data = clamp_size(data, 4096 - 1)  # leave space for fuzzer-added NUL if needed
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets a valid, null-terminated UTF-8 string input.
# The fuzzer stub will take FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and then mask each byte with 0x7F,
# replacing any 0 byte with 'A', and finally appending a terminating NUL.
# Therefore, to steer interesting behavior, we should produce ASCII-only bytes
# (so masking preserves them) and ensure presence/absence of uppercase letters
# to exercise fsearch_string_utf8_has_upper.
# We keep size <= 4096 bytes.

ASCII_UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
ASCII_LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
ASCII_DIGITS = string.digits
ASCII_PUNCT = " !\"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\\]^_`{|}~"

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _rand_len(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(min_len, max_len)


def _make_all_lower(rng: random.Random, ln: int) -> str:
    # Only lowercase ascii to get a clear false case for has_upper
    alphabet = ASCII_LOWER + ASCII_DIGITS + " "
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(ln))


def _make_has_upper_simple(rng: random.Random, ln: int) -> str:
    # Mix of cases; guarantee at least one uppercase
    alphabet = ASCII_LOWER + ASCII_UPPER + ASCII_DIGITS + ASCII_PUNCT
    s = [rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(max(ln, 1))]
    pos = rng.randrange(len(s))
    s[pos] = rng.choice(ASCII_UPPER)
    return "".join(s)


def _make_path_with_extensions(rng: random.Random, ln: int) -> str:
    # Paths/filenames with various dot patterns to exercise extension-like logic
    bases = [
        "file",
        "archive.tar.gz",
        ".hidden",
        "noext",
        "trailingdot.",
        "multi.part.name",
        "UPPER.TXT",
        "MiXeD.CaSe",
    ]
    dirs = ["/usr/local/", "C:/Temp/", "./", "../", ""]
    name = rng.choice(bases)
    # Optionally alter case and add random segments
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        name = name.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else name.lower()
    # Optionally append an extra extension
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ext = rng.choice(["txt", "log", "", "gz", "JPEG", "Md"])  # empty keeps trailing dot case sometimes
        if ext:
            name = f"{name}.{ext}"
        else:
            name = f"{name}."
    # Ensure length target by padding with safe chars
    pad_chars = ASCII_LOWER + ASCII_UPPER + ASCII_DIGITS
    while len(name) < ln and len(name) < 1024:
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            name += "."  # insert more dots
        else:
            name += rng.choice(pad_chars)
    return rng.choice(dirs) + name[:ln]


def _make_wildcard_pattern(rng: random.Random, ln: int) -> str:
    # Patterns involving '*' and '?' and regex metachars to stress conversion
    pieces: List[str] = []
    tokens = [
        "*",
        "?",
        "file",
        "data",
        "IMG",
        "[abc]",   # will be treated as literal in wildcard input; regex escaping interesting
        "(group)",
        ".dot",
        "+plus",
        "^caret",
        "${var}",
    ]
    while sum(len(p) for p in pieces) < ln:
        t = rng.choice(tokens)
        # bias to ensure some uppercase characters
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            t = t.upper()
        pieces.append(t)
    s = "".join(pieces)[:ln]
    # Guarantee at least one wildcard sometimes
    if "*" not in s and "?" not in s and ln > 0 and rng.random() < 0.8:
        i = rng.randrange(len(s))
        s = s[:i] + "*" + s[i+1:]
    return s


def _make_ascii_mixed(rng: random.Random, ln: int) -> str:
    # General mixed ASCII content
    alphabet = ASCII_LOWER + ASCII_UPPER + ASCII_DIGITS + ASCII_PUNCT
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(ln))


def _choose_builder(rng: random.Random):
    # Weighted selection of scenarios to trigger different internal paths
    builders = [
        (0.20, _make_all_lower),            # no uppercase
        (0.30, _make_has_upper_simple),     # has uppercase
        (0.20, _make_path_with_extensions), # dotted names/paths
        (0.20, _make_wildcard_pattern),     # wildcard presence
        (0.10, _make_ascii_mixed),          # general mix
    ]
    r = rng.random()
    acc = 0.0
    for w, b in builders:
        acc += w
        if r <= acc:
            return b
    return builders[-1][1]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Favor small-to-moderate strings but allow up to a few KB
    length = _rand_len(rng, 0, min(512, MAX_SIZE - 1))  # -1 because stub appends NUL
    builder = _choose_builder(rng)
    s = builder(rng, length)

    # Ensure ASCII and avoid interior NULs; though our builders already do this
    # we defensively replace any accidental NULs with 'A'
    s = s.replace("\x00", "A")

    # Bound size to keep total with trailing NUL under MAX_SIZE
    s = s[: max(0, min(len(s), MAX_SIZE - 1))]

    # Return as raw bytes; stub will append NUL terminator itself
    return s.encode('ascii', errors='replace')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid ASCII, null-terminated strings without interior NULs.
# Focus: Exercise fsearch_string_is_ascii_icase and other string utilities semantics.
# - Only 0x01..0x7F characters, no embedded NULs. The fuzzer stub will mask to 7-bit and ensure termination.
# - Provide diverse patterns: mixed case, digits, punctuation, wildcards, paths, dot-files, extensions, intervals, UTF-8-like bytes (clipped to ASCII), etc.
# - Limit size to <= 4096 bytes.

ASCII_MIN = 1
ASCII_MAX = 0x7F
MAX_TOTAL = 4096

SAFE_ASCII = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(ASCII_MIN, ASCII_MAX + 1))
LOWER = string.ascii_lowercase
UPPER = string.ascii_uppercase
DIGITS = string.digits
SPACE = ' '
PUNCT_COMMON = "._-+@#%/,;:()[]{}!$^&=~`'\"|\\"  # all <= 0x7F and non-NUL
WILDCARDS = "*?"


def _rand(rng: random.Random, seq: str, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(seq) for _ in range(n))


def _weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], weights: List[int]) -> str:
    total = sum(weights)
    pick = rng.randrange(total)
    acc = 0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if pick < acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]


def _gen_empty(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return ''


def _gen_lower(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand(rng, LOWER, rng.randint(1, 64))


def _gen_upper(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand(rng, UPPER, rng.randint(1, 64))


def _gen_mixed_case(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(1, 128)
    s = []
    for _ in range(n):
        s.append(rng.choice(LOWER + UPPER))
    return ''.join(s)


def _gen_digits(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand(rng, DIGITS, rng.randint(1, 64))


def _gen_alnum_punct(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(1, 256)
    pool = LOWER + UPPER + DIGITS + PUNCT_COMMON
    return _rand(rng, pool, n)


def _gen_spaces(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(1, 64)
    return ' '.join(_rand(rng, LOWER + UPPER, rng.randint(1, 8)) for _ in range(n))


def _gen_wildcard_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix literal text with '*' and '?'
    parts = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 64)
    for _ in range(count):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.2:
            parts.append('*')
        elif choice < 0.4:
            parts.append('?')
        else:
            parts.append(_rand(rng, LOWER + UPPER + DIGITS + PUNCT_COMMON.replace('*', '').replace('?', ''), rng.randint(1, 6)))
    return ''.join(parts)


def _gen_path_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate UNIX/Windows path-like strings with dots for extensions
    segs = []
    depth = rng.randint(1, 10)
    for i in range(depth):
        base = _rand(rng, LOWER + UPPER + DIGITS + "_-", rng.randint(1, 8))
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            # add extension(s)
            ext_count = 1 + (1 if rng.random() < 0.3 else 0)
            for _ in range(ext_count):
                ext = _rand(rng, LOWER + UPPER + DIGITS, rng.randint(1, 4))
                base += '.' + ext
        segs.append(base)
    prefix = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        prefix = '/'
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        # Windows drive
        drive = rng.choice(UPPER) + ':'
        prefix = drive + ('\\' if rng.random() < 0.5 else '/')
        sep = '\\' if drive and '\\' in prefix else '/'
    sep = '/' if prefix != '' and prefix[-1] == '/' else ('\\' if prefix.endswith('\\') else ('/' if rng.random() < 0.7 else '\\'))
    return prefix + sep.join(segs)


def _gen_dotfiles(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Names that begin with dots to exercise extension parsing rules
    choices = [
        '.bashrc', '.profile', '.config', '.gitignore', '..hidden', '.', '..',
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    return '.' + _rand(rng, LOWER + UPPER + DIGITS + '_-', rng.randint(0, 8))


def _gen_tricky_dots(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    patterns = [
        'file.',
        'file..',
        '.file',
        'a.b.c',
        '...many...dots...',
    ]
    return rng.choice(patterns)


def _gen_interval_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Strings starting with ".." or "-" to exercise interval detection
    start = rng.choice(['..', '-'])
    tail = _rand(rng, LOWER + UPPER + DIGITS + PUNCT_COMMON, rng.randint(0, 64))
    return start + tail


def _gen_ascii_full_range(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build from almost full ASCII (excluding NUL). Include control chars 0x01..0x1F and DEL 0x7F.
    # Ensure some controls are present.
    controls = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(1, 32)) + chr(127)
    visibles = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127))
    n = rng.randint(1, 512)
    pool = controls + visibles
    s = _rand(rng, pool, n)
    # Avoid interior NUL already; ensure at least one control sometimes
    if not any(ord(ch) < 32 or ord(ch) == 127 for ch in s) and n > 1 and rng.random() < 0.7:
        idx = rng.randrange(n)
        s = s[:idx] + rng.choice(controls) + s[idx+1:]
    return s


def _cap_length(s: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Ensure final byte length <= 4096 (fuzzer adds one for NUL terminator)
    max_len = MAX_TOTAL - 1
    if len(s) <= max_len:
        return s
    # Prefer trimming at boundaries like separators or spaces
    cut = rng.randint(max_len // 2, max_len)
    return s[:cut]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a generator with weights to cover a wide variety
    gens = [
        _gen_empty,
        _gen_lower,
        _gen_upper,
        _gen_mixed_case,
        _gen_digits,
        _gen_alnum_punct,
        _gen_spaces,
        _gen_wildcard_pattern,
        _gen_path_like,
        _gen_dotfiles,
        _gen_tricky_dots,
        _gen_interval_prefix,
        _gen_ascii_full_range,
    ]
    weights = [
        2,  # empty
        6,  # lower
        4,  # upper
        8,  # mixed
        4,  # digits
        8,  # general ascii word/punct
        3,  # spaces
        6,  # wildcards
        6,  # paths
        4,  # dotfiles
        4,  # tricky dots
        5,  # interval prefix
        6,  # full ascii range (no NUL)
    ]

    # Optionally concatenate multiple segments to create more complex strings
    seg_count = 1 + (1 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0) + (1 if rng.random() < 0.2 else 0)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(seg_count):
        g = _weighted_choice(rng, gens, weights)
        parts.append(g(rng))
        # Occasionally insert separators or wildcards between segments
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(rng.choice(['', ' ', '/', '\\', '.', '-', '_', '*', '?']))
    s = ''.join(parts)

    # Ensure only 0x01..0x7F and no interior NULs
    filtered_chars = []
    for ch in s:
        a = ord(ch) & 0x7F
        if a == 0:
            # replace NUL with a safe ASCII letter
            a = ord('a')
        filtered_chars.append(chr(a))
    s = ''.join(filtered_chars)

    s = _cap_length(s, rng)

    # Return as bytes; C++ stub appends a NUL terminator
    return s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid wildcard pattern strings suitable for:
# - fsearch_string_has_wildcards
# - fsearch_string_convert_wildcard_to_regex_expression
#
# Goals:
# - Always produce a valid null-terminated C string buffer (bytes ending with \0).
# - Include a wide variety of patterns: with/without wildcards, edge cases, regex metacharacters
#   (., [], (), {}, +, ^, $, |, \\) that should be treated as literals by wildcard-to-regex conversion.
# - Cover path-like inputs, filenames with dots, leading dots, multiple dots, trailing dots, ranges, etc.
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.

ASCII_PRINTABLE_NO_NUL = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127) if c != '\\0')
SAFE_LITERALS = ''.join(ch for ch in ASCII_PRINTABLE_NO_NUL if ch not in '*?')
REGEX_META = ".^$|()[]{}+\\"
PATH_SEPS = "/\\\\"

PREMADE_PATTERNS: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty string
    "*",  # only wildcard
    "?",  # single-char wildcard
    "**",  # repeated wildcard
    "???",  # multiple ?
    "*.txt",
    "file?.txt",
    "image_*_v?.png",
    "*.tar.gz",
    "backup_202?-??-??.zip",
    "report-2023-*-final.pdf",
    "[literal].txt",  # regex metacharacters as literals in wildcard space
    ".bashrc",  # leading dot filename
    "...",  # only dots
    "file.",  # trailing dot
    "no_wildcards_here",
    "path/with/subdir/*/file?.ext",
    "C:/Windows/*/System32/?.dll",
    "./*",
    "../*.c",
    "\\\\server\\share\\*",
    "{not_regex}_file.txt",
    "(paren).*?+^$|.txt",  # rich regex metas to escape
    "data-[0-9]?.csv",  # pseudo range
    "*.*",
    "*?*?*.?",
    "??????????",
]

WORDS = [
    "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "epsilon", "zeta", "eta", "theta",
    "report", "final", "draft", "backup", "image", "video", "music",
    "config", "system", "kernel", "module", "driver", "plugin",
]
EXTS = ["txt", "md", "csv", "json", "xml", "html", "log", "gz", "tar.gz", "png", "jpg", "dll", "so"]


def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def make_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    leading = "" if rng.random() < 0.7 else rand_choice(rng, PATH_SEPS)
    for i in range(depth):
        base = rand_choice(rng, WORDS)
        # sprinkle wildcards or literals
        mode = rng.random()
        if mode < 0.25:
            base = base + ("*" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "?")
        elif mode < 0.5:
            base = base + rand_choice(rng, [".", "-", "_"]) + rand_choice(rng, WORDS)
        elif mode < 0.65:
            base = base + rand_choice(rng, ["[", "]", "(", ")", "+", "^", "$", "|", "."]).replace("\\", "")
        parts.append(base)
    fname = make_filename(rng)
    return leading + (rand_choice(rng, PATH_SEPS).join(parts + [fname]) if parts else fname)


def make_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rand_choice(rng, WORDS)
    # Optionally add wildcards into base
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        insert_pos = rng.randint(0, len(base))
        base = base[:insert_pos] + rand_choice(rng, ["*", "?"]) + base[insert_pos:]
    # Optionally add another segment and dot patterns
    tail = ""
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        ext = rand_choice(rng, EXTS)
        # Possibly complex extension like "tar.gz" already handled
        tail = "." + ext
    elif rng.random() < 0.5:
        # multiple dots cases
        tail = "." * rng.randint(1, 3)
    # Possibly leading dot filename
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        base = "." + base
    return base + tail


def inject_regex_meta(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Ensure presence of regex metacharacters that the converter should escape
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        metas = [".", "[", "]", "(", ")", "+", "^", "$", "|", "\\"]
        # place 1-4 metas at varied positions
        n = rng.randint(1, 4)
        for _ in range(n):
            pos = rng.randint(0, len(s))
            s = s[:pos] + rand_choice(rng, metas) + s[pos:]
    return s


def build_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a strategy to create a pattern
    p = rng.random()
    if p < 0.25:
        s = rand_choice(rng, PREMADE_PATTERNS)
    elif p < 0.55:
        s = make_path(rng)
    else:
        # Construct from tokens
        tokens = []
        n = rng.randint(1, 6)
        for _ in range(n):
            t = rng.random()
            if t < 0.25:
                tokens.append("*")
            elif t < 0.5:
                tokens.append("?")
            elif t < 0.7:
                # literal word or number run
                word = rand_choice(rng, WORDS)
                if rng.random() < 0.4:
                    word += str(rng.randint(0, 9999))
                tokens.append(word)
            else:
                # regex metachar or dot-separated segment
                piece = rand_choice(rng, [".", "-", "_", "(", ")", "[", "]", "+", "^", "$", "|"])
                tokens.append(piece)
        s = ''.join(tokens)
        # Optionally add extension
        if rng.random() < 0.6 and not s.endswith('.'):
            s += "." + rand_choice(rng, EXTS)
    # Occasionally force no wildcards to exercise negative path
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_LITERALS) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 20)))
    # Sprinkle extra regex metas to test escaping in converter
    s = inject_regex_meta(rng, s)
    # Cap total length
    return s[:4000] if len(s) > 4000 else s


def to_c_string_bytes(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure ASCII bytes; since library expects C string, and behavior on non-ASCII is unspecified for ASCII functions,
    # keep to ASCII. Replace any accidental NULs just in case, then append NUL terminator.
    s = s.replace('\x00', '')
    b = s.encode('ascii', 'ignore')
    if len(b) > 4095:
        b = b[:4095]
    return b + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly pick between a small set of highly specific edge cases and a synthesized pattern
    edge_cases = [
        b"\x00",  # empty C string
        b"*.txt\x00",
        b"?\x00",
        b"*.*\x00",
        b"file.\x00",  # trailing dot
        b".bashrc\x00",  # leading dot
        b"no_wildcards\x00",
        b"(paren).*?+^$|.txt\x00",
        b"path/with/[brackets]?\x00",
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        return rand_choice(rng, edge_cases)
    pattern = build_pattern(rng)
    return to_c_string_bytes(pattern)
